posts.text:
🇺🇸🇮🇷 WHAT IF Trump is avoiding another attack on Iran because America itself is TOO VULNERABLE to retaliation?

Brandon Weichert spoke with former Pentagon official and military strategist David Pyne about the U.S. blockade, the recent wave of infrastructure disruptions, and why Washington may be running out of good options.

David believes Iran could be using cyberattacks to send Trump a message: hit our power grid, and we might hit yours.

He suspects Tehran is behind at least some of the recent U.S. disruptions, although there's no confirmed evidence linking Iran to those incidents.

And the potential consequences are enormous.

America depends on interconnected banking, electricity, water and transportation systems. David argues that a serious cyberattack could cause far more damage here than a comparable American operation against Iran.

Meanwhile, the blockade isn't delivering the quick victory Trump promised.

David cited an alleged CIA assessment suggesting Tehran could potentially withstand the economic pressure until 2029.

That's THREE more years of a blockade that may never force Iran to surrender.

We also discussed reports of North Korean military advisers operating alongside the Houthis in Yemen. Those reports remain unverified, but David believes Pyongyang could be extending its military cooperation with Iran into another battlefield.

And he sees a possible diplomatic exit.

Following Trump's meetings with Putin and Xi, David believes Washington could pursue a deal involving Iran's enriched uranium, allowing Trump to declare victory without launching another offensive.

The irony is that Trump may have more to gain from negotiating with America's rivals than from continuing to threaten Iran.

America has the firepower to escalate this war. What it doesn't have is a convincing way to win it.
